original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-koszul-independence-presentation}
Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map. If for some presentation
$\alpha : A[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B$ the kernel $I$ is a Koszul-regular ideal
then for any presentation $\beta : A[y_1, \ldots, y_m] \to B$ the kernel
$J$ is a Koszul-regular ideal.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 8259 says if ONE finite polynomial presentation of a finite-type A→B has Koszul-regular kernel then EVERY such presentation does. Both existence and universality are preserved.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-lci-local}
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. Let $g_1, \ldots, g_m \in S$
generate the unit ideal. If each $R \to S_{g_j}$ is a local
complete intersection so is $R \to S$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 8347 states the lci property is local on a finite principal open cover of S given by elements generating 1. The draft preserves the requirement all R→S_gj are lci.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-koszul}
Let $R$ be a ring. If $R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$
is a relative global complete intersection, then $f_1, \ldots, f_c$
is a Koszul regular sequence.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 8385 assumes a polynomial quotient by f_i is a RELATIVE GLOBAL complete intersection and concludes f_i Koszul-regular; no converse or Noetherian hypothesis is added.
